gapTheirs: Tighter monospace advance: 25.6 px per cell against B's 26.0 px (1.6% narrower). Both rows come out 26 px shorter (the 'Teh' mark starts at x=1048 vs 1066), and the heavier stems plus the tighter pitch make 'on Tuesday,' and 'noon. Teh' look a little crowded.
verdict: The spell mark itself is identical in both, measured to the pixel: round #ED766B dots 6 px across on an 8 px period, rows y=47–52 and y=121–126, with 'definately' and 'comittee' marked over 254 px and 'Teh' over 78 px, and DRAFFT left unmarked in both. So the choice comes down to the prose above the dots. A's text is darker and sharper and holds the page. Nobody would switch apps over this, but after an hour you'd feel B's softness before you noticed A's tightness.

states.name: on-dark
states.gap: A's glyphs are bigger than B's while the dots sit in the same place, so the gap between text and mark shrinks. The ink of row 1 runs y=4–44 in A against y=6–43 in B, about 40 px tall against 37 px, and advances 26.0 px per cell against B's ~25.6. The dot row sits at y=47–52 in both, so the descender of the 'y' in 'definately' clears the dots by 2 px in A and 3 px in B. The same passage also comes out 26 px wider (1664 vs 1638).
states.gapTheirs: B's dots have a faint halo. Each 6 px dot has a soft #1E1E1E–#7F5352 fringe on rows 47 and 52, where A draws a hard 4 px core with a single #845655 edge pixel. At reading distance B's dots are a touch fuzzier. Colour, period and depth are the same in both: peak #CF7x7x, 8 px period, y=47–52.
states.verdict: The two marks are the same row of round dots in the same muted red, 6 px wide on an 8 px period and the same depth under the baseline. Neither one is a wave, and neither ever flashes like a browser squiggle. The difference is how the letters sit on the dots. A's slightly larger face pushes its descenders to within 2 px of the dots, so 'definately' reads as heavy. B leaves a little more air and sets the line tighter, so it feels calmer. You would only notice after an hour of revising, but you would notice.
secondary: The images are different sizes: A is 1664x135 and B is 1638x135. Crop height matches, but the width follows the cell advance (26.0 vs ~25.6 px).
Both images mark 'definately', 'recieved', 'comittee' and 'Teh', and neither marks 'DRAFFT'.

Dot runs hug the words the same way: 'definately' ink 366–620 has dots 364–617 in A, and ink 360–610 has dots 358–611 in B. In A the dots stop 3 px short of the 'y' tail; in B they overshoot it by 1 px.
Row 2 dots: 'comittee' 494–699 and 'Teh' 1066–1143 in A, against 486–691 and 1048–1125 in B. The drift comes only from the cell advance.
Dot peak ink is #CF in the red channel in both, and neither shows alpha dimming against the #1A1A1A background.
The body text is the same grey #C6–#CF in both, with no weight difference visible at 4x zoom.

states.name: focus-light
states.gap: B's dots don't line up with the words. Under 'definately' they run x≈364–618 but the glyphs run x≈366–621: they start 2 px early and stop about 3 px short of the 'y'. That's 32 dots at the 8 px period (256 px) under a 26 px advance (260 px). A's 25.6 px advance gives the same 256 px, so its dots start and stop with the glyphs (358–612 vs 360–611). The same short ending shows under 'recieved', 'comittee' and 'Teh'.
states.gapTheirs: A has a stray blue half-disc about 12 px wide at x≈47–54, y≈128–135 under the first letters of row 2. It is something foreign cut off by the crop, and B's bottom edge is clean #F7F7F7. The dots, the dim ink (#C6C4C2) and the black (#191919) are the same in both.
states.verdict: The two agree on everything that matters: round dots, not a wave, in #ED766B, with a 1 px lighter ring, set the same distance below the text, and the dots stay bright on the dimmed sentence. B's mark doesn't match the word it sits under. It starts a hair left of the first letter and stops short of the last, so a writer looking for the end of a misspelling sees it end early. A's dots start and stop with the letters, which is why it wins, but only just.
secondary: Image sizes differ: A is 1638x135, B is 1664x135. That's 26 px wider for B, which matches 26.0 vs 25.6 px per character over about 64 characters.
Dots in both: about 6 px across, 8 px apart, 3 px tall (rows 48–51), top about 12 px below the baseline; A's run is 6 px tall overall vs B's 9 px when trimmed.
DRAFFT has no mark in either; Teh is marked in the focused sentence in both.
B's letters look a touch heavier at the same size, probably from different rendering or hinting.
Dimmed text is #C6C4C2 on #F7F7F7 in both, only about 1.6:1 contrast, so the dots are the loudest thing in the dimmed sentence.

states.name: focus-dark
states.gap: B's text is set looser: 1664 px against 1638 px for the same two rows, which works out to about 26.0 against 25.6 px per character (+1.6%). Its dots also have harder edges: the faded edge pixel of each 6 px dot is #845655 in B against #C27A78 in A, so B's dots look like small clipped octagons, not soft round beads.
states.gapTheirs: A blue caret tip (about 4 px, pure blue up to 250) pokes into the bottom edge at x≈50, y≈132. The caret line is cut off by the crop, so the frame shows a stray coloured fleck under the prose that B doesn't have.
states.verdict: You would struggle to tell these apart. The dot mark is the same in both: 6 px dots every 8 px, sitting on the same rows (y 47–52 and 121–126), in the same #CF807E, under the same dim #707070 text, with DRAFFT left unmarked. What separates them is texture. B's line runs 26 px wider and its dots have a hard edge where A's fade softly, so B's error mark reads a little more like a stitched line than a quiet row of dots. A is the page a writer would settle into, but only just.

states.name: syntax-light
states.gap: The syntax colours disagree on 4 words in row 2: 'comittee' and 'Teh' are plain near-black text in A but orange nouns in B; 'DRAFFT' is black in A and brown/ochre in B; 'before' is green in A and uncoloured in B. So in A, 2 of the 4 marked words lose their word-class colour and look like function words, while the dots under them look exactly the same as B's.
states.gapTheirs: B leaves 'before' as plain black text where A colours it green (a function word). B also colours 'DRAFFT' in a fifth, brown-ochre colour, which spell check leaves alone, so the unmarked word draws the eye more than the marked words next to it. Otherwise it matches A.
states.verdict: The dots are identical in both: #ed766b, the same four ink rows (48–51 in row 1, 47–50 in row 2), the same row counts and the same stretch relative to each word. Nobody could tell them apart on the mark alone. The choice comes down to syntax colour: A turns 'comittee' and 'Teh' black, so a misspelled noun in A looks like an article with a rash, while B keeps the noun colour under the dots. B only wins narrowly, because its uncoloured 'before' and the loud ochre on 'DRAFFT' are debatable calls of their own.
secondary: The images are different widths: A is 1664x135 and B is 1638x135. That's 26 px, which fits a cell advance of 26.0 vs 25.6 over about 64 columns.
The dots are exactly the same: round, about 6 px across, 4 px tall, spaced about 8 px apart, in #ED766B with a #EE7D73/#ED7D74 anti-aliased edge.

The glyph ink in A starts about 2 px higher and runs about 2 px taller in the first-row crop (49 px vs 47 px). This is a small difference in font rendering or baseline.
Neither image shows a caret, a selection or dimming, so the rule that the mark does not dim can't be judged from this state.

states.verdict: The spell marks match to the pixel in both: the same #CF807E round dots, 11 under 'Teh', a band 4 px tall, the same drop below the baseline, and none under DRAFFT. The real difference is what happens to a misspelled word under Syntax highlight. B still colours it by its part of speech, but A turns 'comittee' and 'Teh' grey, as if the typo had taken them out of the grammar. A's cells are also about 1.5% wider, so its rows are 26 px longer and look looser. Neither is bad, but B is the one whose highlighting I'd trust while revising.

states.name: select-light
states.gap: B's dots sit closer to the letters. Under 'definately', 2 px of clear space separates the y descender (ink ends at y=45) from the dots (y=47–52); A leaves 3 px. On a word with descenders the mark in B nearly touches the word it flags. B's crop is also 26 px wider (1664 vs 1638) for the same words, so the lines run a little longer.
states.gapTheirs: Under the held selection the dots change colour and B's don't. On 'recieved', A's dot cores go from #ED766B to #E2726B, darker and muddier where they sit on the #CBEDF7 band, as if the mark were blended with the selection. B's dots stay at #ED766B on the band, the same as off it. A's type is also smaller: 'definately' measures 38 px of ink from ascender to descender in A against 41 px in B, and the selection band starts at y=57 in A against y=60 in B, so the lines sit 3 px higher.
states.verdict: The two marks are almost the same: round dots 6 px across on an 8 px period, red #ED766B, marking the same four words and leaving DRAFFT unmarked. A slips in one place: the dots get darker under the selection, so 'recieved the notes' looks slightly bruised just when you are about to fix it. B's type is a size larger and its mark stays one colour on and off the selection, but its dots crowd the descenders. Neither would stop me writing; B's mark behaves the same everywhere, and that is what you need from a spell-check mark.

A's tighter spacing lines the dots up with the words, and that is the only reason to pick it.
